item.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78670-y

DSBs are repaired by NHEJ or HR. Using reconstituted reactions with purified yeast proteins, the authors show that DNA end synapsis blocks short-range resection, giving NHEJ time to ligate. Moreover, RPA promotes HR by stimulating the exonuclease of MRXpSae2 and allowing Ku removal from DNA ends.
item.dc:title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair

item.title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78018-6

Here, the authors observe magneto-photoluminescence intensity oscillations in exciton and biexciton peaks of twisted bilayer MoS2, interpreted as optical Aharonov-Bohm interference with harmonic frequency hierarchy linked to the moiré-cell area.
item.dc:title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes

item.title: Enhancing bosonic qubit protection by squeezing
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78025-7

In bosonic codes, decoherence can be seen as the environment performing an unwanted measurement on a noise-sensitive quadrature, collapsing superpositions and inducing errors. Here, the authors show how to use squeezing to further protect bosonic codes from noise, extending the bit-flip times of the cat qubit by two orders of magnitude without reducing phase-flip times.
item.dc:title: Enhancing bosonic qubit protection by squeezing

item.title: A porous solid electrolyte interface enables efficient electroreduction of captured carbon to CO
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78954-3

Turning captured carbon dioxide into useful chemicals can save energy, but combining capture and conversion is difficult. Here, the authors report a membrane reactor converts bicarbonate solutions directly into carbon monoxide with high carbon efficiency and lower energy use.
item.dc:title: A porous solid electrolyte interface enables efficient electroreduction of captured carbon to CO

item.title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78644-0

Gallstone disease is common, but its genetic basis remains incompletely understood. Here, the authors conduct a trans‑ancestry GWAS identifying 116 risk loci, linking gallstone susceptibility to lipid and liver metabolism pathways and expanding understanding of disease biology across diverse populations.
item.dc:title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease

item.title: Determining depth-resolved spatial distribution of solid–electrolyte interphase using non-destructive angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy for lithium-metal batteries
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78168-7

Understanding the solid–electrolyte interphase formed on lithium is vital for improving the lifetime of lithium metal batteries. Here, authors show that angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy can reveal the depth-dependent composition of the interfacial layer without damaging it by ion sputtering.
item.dc:title: Determining depth-resolved spatial distribution of solid–electrolyte interphase using non-destructive angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy for lithium-metal batteries

item.title: Ocean acidification, reduced silicate availability and declines in Ocean productivity
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78463-3

Long-term CO2-generated declines in ocean pH block recycling of silicon, an essential nutrient for diatom-driven ocean production. Associated reductions in chlorophyll and plankton-feeding fish reveal a novel CO2 impact on marine ecosystem health.
item.dc:title: Ocean acidification, reduced silicate availability and declines in Ocean productivity
